inherited_rule_queue.actual_assertion: Apply the source-of-profit analysis under section 11 and Schedule 1, not a blanket worldwide or tax-free-offshore assumption. The standard company rate is 15% from 1 July 2024. The higher rate is 20% for the statutory utility/dominant-position categories. Mixed activities require classification before rates are assigned. Rule 6(3) requires the Commissioner's opinion that the company has abused its dominant market position; market dominance alone is not the complete statutory condition. [ITO, Guidance Notes for Companies, August 2025, pp2–3](https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/uploads/Income%20Tax%20Office/Corporate/Guidance%20Notes%20for%20Companies,%2008-2025.pdf); [Income Tax Act](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).

inherited_rule_queue.old_heading: Company residence and the source of profits
inherited_rule_queue.actual_assertion: Section 74 defines an ordinarily resident company by **management and control in Gibraltar**, or management and control exercised outside Gibraltar by persons ordinarily resident in Gibraltar. It adds a control rule for investment companies, including power through shares, votes or constitutional documents to secure that affairs follow the resident controller's wishes. “Investment company” here concerns a company whose income mainly falls outside trade, business or employment profits. Do not replace these tests with place of incorporation alone. Collect the decision-making history, directors' and controllers' residence, constitutional powers and actual conduct; no single meeting or registered address settles the factual analysis. [Section 74, company residence and investment-company definitions](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).

inherited_rule_queue.old_heading: Company residence and the source of profits
inherited_rule_queue.actual_assertion: Residence and source answer different questions. Section 11(1) charges the specified Schedule 1 income accruing in or derived from Gibraltar. Section 11(2)'s additional charge on specified foreign income of ordinarily resident persons expressly excludes companies. That does not create an exemption for every foreign receipt of a company: apply the statutory source definition and the interest, royalty and movable-property deeming rules below. [Section 11(1)–(2); Schedule 1, Table C](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).

inherited_rule_queue.old_heading: Company residence and the source of profits
inherited_rule_queue.actual_assertion: Under section 74, source is determined by the location of the activities giving rise to profits. The definition also deems those activities to take place in Gibraltar where the underlying income-producing activity requires licensing and regulation under Gibraltar law, or falls within the specified lawful passporting branch/permanent-establishment case. A foreign customer, overseas payment account or contract signature abroad is therefore not by itself a non-chargeability test. For example, a Gibraltar team supplying services to an overseas customer must analyse its profit-producing work rather than classify the invoice as exempt because the customer is abroad. [Section 74, definition of accrued in and derived from](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).

inherited_rule_queue.old_heading: UK treaty: permanent establishments and business profits
inherited_rule_queue.actual_assertion: Apply this section only after establishing entitlement under the UK–Gibraltar agreement, its effective period and Article 4 residence. For dual-resident companies, authority agreement is required for relief except to the extent authorities otherwise agree; incorporation alone is not the treaty tie-breaker. See [UK treaty entitlement](gi-uk-investment-income-treaty.md). Items separately dealt with elsewhere in the agreement retain their own rules under Article 7(4); absence of a PE is not a universal exemption for property income or investment payments. inherited_rule_queue.old_heading: UK treaty: permanent establishments and business profits > Fixed places and projects
inherited_rule_queue.actual_assertion: Article 5(1) defines a PE as a fixed business location through which the enterprise conducts all or part of its business. Paragraph (2) lists management places, branches, offices, factories, workshops and natural-resource extraction locations. It is not a twelve-month grace period for every office, agent or other business activity. Verify project start, completion, interruptions and any aggregation issue before drawing a conclusion; the text alone does not settle every project-timing fact. [Article 5(1)–(3)](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/gibraltar-tax-treaties/2019-uk-gibraltar-double-taxation-agreement-in-force#article-5-permanent-establishment).

Schedule 1 Table C Class 1A covers loan/advance interest between companies and deems it Gibraltar-source where the recipient company is registered in Gibraltar. The exclusion applies where interest from any one company is **less than £100,000 per annum**. For this threshold, interest from companies connected with each other under Schedule 4 paragraph 9 is aggregated. The rule does not require the borrower and lender themselves to be connected before inter-company interest can fall within Class 1A. [Schedule 1, Table C, Class 1A](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).

inherited_rule_queue.old_heading: Establish the tax accounting periods
inherited_rule_queue.actual_assertion: Section 16 starts a company's tax accounting period when it is first registered in Gibraltar or when the preceding accounting period ends. It normally ends at the earlier of twelve months from its beginning and the company's accounting date. Do not automatically use trading commencement as the first tax-period start, or assume a long set of financial statements creates one equally long tax period. Retain the registration evidence, accounting-date history and prior assessments. [Section 16(1)–(3)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).

inherited_rule_queue.old_heading: Establish the tax accounting periods
inherited_rule_queue.actual_assertion: Winding up ends an accounting period and begins another at its commencement, subject to section 16(1)–(3). inherited_rule_queue.old_heading: Establish the tax accounting periods
inherited_rule_queue.actual_assertion: For accounts exceeding twelve months, subsection (6) requires time apportionment on the basis that profits accrued evenly. Its wording identifies an initial period ending on the company's accounting date and a subsequent period comprising the remaining twelve months. **Do not substitute a standard first-twelve-months-plus-remainder convention without confirming the applicable boundaries.** Obtain the determined periods and reconcile allocated profits to the accounts. If a confirmed allocation divides £180,000 evenly over eighteen months into six- and twelve-month periods, the amounts are £60,000 and £120,000; this arithmetic does not determine which dates apply. Subsection (7) gives the Commissioner discretion over profit allocation if an accounting-date delay beyond twelve months was effected to reduce tax. [Section 16(6)–(7)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).

The latter exception also has a statutory exclusion following refused claims in three of the preceding ten years, lasting the specified five-year period. inherited_rule_queue.old_heading: Capital allowances: equipment purchases and pools
